sections.heading: Cursor buyer question and thesis
sections.body:
LLM chat and assistants; reasoning / advanced models; writing and paraphrasing; agent / app builder. Hobby · free · LLM chat and assistants | Pro | Teams Standard. Developers who want an AI-native editor rather than a plugin; Teams running Agent-heavy refactors with MCP/tools; Orgs ready for Teams SSO and privacy modes. Cursor is an AI-native code editor (VS Code fork) with Tab completions, Agent, Cloud Agents, and MCP/skills. Hobby is free with limited Agent/Tab. Pro is list price. Teams Standard. That catalogue mix is the Cursor setup filter — not a generic ai lecture.

Buyer question: choose Cursor only if Developers who want an AI-native editor rather than a plugin outweighs Switching editors is a real adoption cost vs Copilot-in-VS-Code — otherwise keep researching.

Verdict shape: yes for teams built around Developers who want an AI-native editor rather than a plugin; Teams running Agent-heavy refactors with MCP/tools; Orgs ready for Teams SSO and privacy modes; no when Teams that refuse to leave VS Code/JetBrains + Copilot plugin; Procurement that only wants GitHub Enterprise Copilot SKUs; Non-coding LLM chat (ChatGPT / Perplexity) — LLM chat and assistants is the hinge, not brand familiarity.

Best for: Developers who want an AI-native editor rather than a plugin; Teams running Agent-heavy refactors with MCP/tools; Orgs ready for Teams SSO and privacy modes (Developers who want an AI-native editor rather than a plugin).

Poor fit when: Teams that refuse to leave VS Code/JetBrains + Copilot plugin; Procurement that only wants GitHub Enterprise Copilot SKUs; Non-coding LLM chat (ChatGPT / Perplexity). Avoid if Switching editors is a real adoption cost vs Copilot-in-VS-Code would block go-live.

sections.heading: Cursor limitation, pricing interpretation, and alternative context
sections.body:
Limitation: Switching editors is a real adoption cost vs Copilot-in-VS-Code; Usage overage on Agent/frontier models can exceed list price Pro; Enterprise controls are sales-gated because it forces process changes or add-ons around Cursor when LLM chat and assistants is the job.

Pricing interpretation: stay on Hobby until LLM chat and assistants is mandatory; plan jumps to Pro only after that hinge is proven.

Plan trade-off: you gain LLM chat and assistants at the expense of Published free tiers vs paid usage/credit caps — measure both in the pilot. Researched packaging: Hobby · free · LLM chat and assistants | Pro | Teams Standard.

Alternative context: unlike GitHub Copilot, Cursor is preferable when Developers who want an AI-native editor rather than a plugin because LLM chat and assistants plus LLM chat and assistants match; prefer GitHub Copilot when Teams that refuse to leave VS Code/JetBrains + Copilot plugin because the operating loops differ.

sections.heading: Decision scenario and conclusion for Cursor
sections.body:
Scenario: for LLM chat and assistants teams, recommend Cursor when Developers who want an AI-native editor rather than a plugin; recommend an alternative path when Teams that refuse to leave VS Code/JetBrains + Copilot plugin because Switching editors is a real adoption cost vs Copilot-in-VS-Code dominates.

Implementation effort: setup takes a named admin for LLM chat and assistants plus a freeze window if Slack are in the cutover path.

Final call: proceed with Cursor when LLM chat and assistants plus LLM chat and assistants outweigh Switching editors is a real adoption cost vs Copilot-in-VS-Code; walk when Teams that refuse to leave VS Code/JetBrains + Copilot plugin because workarounds will eat the Pro spend.
